items.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Gerald stayed around in town, the next thing he knew he was gone to Chicago to join Jimmie Lunceford‘s band, Gerald Wilson. ... He replaced the guy who wrote a lot of music for Jimmie Lunceford

ctx.x: Yes…because you left home, you said, in the tenth grade you left school.
I must have been, I went with Jimmie when I was nineteen, so I must have been fifteen or sixteen years old when I went with Chick.
And how long were you in Chick Carter‘s band?

items.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee refers to 'Jimmy' as his brother James Young. The person to judge is 'Jimmy Lunceford'. The transcript contains no mention of a relationship between the interviewee (Young Snooky/Eugene Edward Young) and Jimmy Lunceford.

ctx.x: Yes, I have. There was seven of us in my family, four boys and three girls. My oldest brother was Granville, Granville Young. I was the second, no I wasn‘t second, my sister was second, Mary-Louise, and then I was third; Eugene Edward Young. The fourth child was, was it Ursabelle? I think it was Ursabelle. It‘s hard for me to remember of my sisters and brothers now it‘s been so many years. Ursabelle and then Jimmy; James Young. And then my youngest brother was Don Young. I think that was all seven of my sisters…
Judy, go ahead, you can make an addendum. Judy Andrews: Joanne…
